No film exists of the Wright brothers' first flight at Kitty Hawk in 1903 — only a photograph. This is the closest thing: U.S. Army Signal Corps film of the Wright Military Flyer trials at Fort Myer, Virginia, in 1908–1909, where the Army tested and then bought the world's first military airplane. The Flyer had no wheels — a falling counterweight slung it down a launch rail, with Orville Wright at the controls. The 1908 trials ended in the crash that killed Lieutenant Thomas Selfridge, the first person ever to die in an airplane accident; Orville, badly injured, rebuilt and returned in 1909. The surviving reel is a 1930s Signal Corps compilation mixing 1908 and 1909 material, and the National Archives holds it as its oldest known government-produced film.
 
 Original film: U.S. Army Signal Corps, "First Army Aeroplane Flight, Fort Myer, Virginia" (National Archives Identifier 24690). US government work, public domain.
 Narration is an AI voice. Score, ambience, and engine sound are modern reconstructions — the film is silent.

The President Filmed the Day Before He Was Shot

The President Filmed the Day Before He Was Shot President William McKinley speaking at the Pan-American Exposition in Buffalo, New York, on September 5, 1901 — filmed by Thomas Edison's motion picture company, which had cameras on him throughout the visit. The next afternoon, September 6, he was shot at close range while shaking hands with the public inside the Exposition's Temple of Music. Edison's crew had set up outside the building to film the President walking out; the shooting meant that picture was never made. McKinley died on September 14. The film closes with his funeral procession in Washington, D.C., September 17, 1901. #history #mckinley #archivalfootage #1901 #edison #shorts

This Was Filmed 4 Days Before San Francisco Burned A camera bolted to the front of a cable car, hand-cranked all the way down Market Street from Eighth Street to the Ferry Building — San Francisco, April 14, 1906. Four days later, at 5:12 a.m. on April 18, the earthquake struck. The First Video Ever Recorded — And The Man Who Filmed It Vanished The oldest surviving film in the world: two seconds shot on 14 October 1888 in the garden of Oakwood Grange in Roundhay, Leeds, England — seven years before the Lumière brothers held their first public screening in Paris. The four people walking in circles are Adolphe Le Prince, Harriet Hartley, Joseph Whitley, and Sarah Whitley. Sarah, in the dark dress, died ten days later, on 24 October 1888 — the first person ever captured on film to die. #history #film #truecrime #unsolved #archivalfootage #1888 #cinema #mystery #shorts

The Only Video of Mark Twain That Exists

The Only Video of Mark Twain That Exists The only known motion picture of Mark Twain — filmed in 1909 at Stormfield, his estate in Redding, Connecticut, by Thomas Edison's film company. The women at the tea table are believed to be his daughters, Clara and Jean. Jean died that December; Twain followed seven months later, the day after Halley's Comet returned — just as he'd always predicted. #history #marktwain #archivalfootage #vintage #edison #shorts
